_meta.what: Corrections to the subject shown above a question.
_meta.why: categorize.ts picks the globally RAREST of a bill's candidate categories. 52 of the 54 quiz bills with more than one candidate got the rarest, which for a multi-subject bill is systematically the least representative one.
_meta.rule: A proposed category MUST be one of that bill's own candidate categories, derived from its official subject list at capitol.texas.gov. scripts/fix_categories.mjs refuses anything else, so a correction can only pick a different subject the Legislature itself assigned.

HB 5138.reason: The bill gives the attorney general power to prosecute election-law crimes when a local prosecutor has not acted. Abortion is genuinely one of its ten official subjects, but the operative effect is entirely election law, and 'Abortion' above this question tells a reader something false about what they are voting on.

SB 5.reason: Creates a state institute funding dementia prevention and research. Health & Human Services is among its official subjects. Not visible on the card — SB 5 is a headline bill and carries its own label — but the category still decides which real-world outcome is revealed after the question.

HB 1784.reason: Extends the support colleges must give former foster-care students to students who are homeless. Its subjects include higher education; Religion & Civil Liberties has no outcome attached at all, so the question currently reveals nothing after it.

HB 145.reason: Electric utility wildfire liability and risk plans. Energy & Environment is among its official subjects and is what the bill is about.

HB 5596.reason: Changes the voter-approval tax rate for coastal cities that misspent hotel occupancy tax revenue. Both are official subjects; the bill is a tax measure.

HB 5246.reason: Texas Space Commission, aerospace research, the space economy consortium, and abolishing the spaceport trust fund. Military & Veterans is a real tag but incidental. The subject list names ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT & TOURISM OFFICE, TEXAS alongside Economic & Industrial Development and Business & Commerce — the aerospace office sits inside economic development — which is why Business & Labor over Transportation, the other defensible candidate (Aeronautics, Transportation--Aviation).
HB 5246.note: The one judgement call of the six. Flip 'proposed' to 'Transportation' and re-run if you read it the other way.
